newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rains help refresh Brazil soybean regions.
newsitem.headline: Rains help refresh Brazil soybean regions.

text.p: Rains over the weekend in soybean-growing regions of Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul state have helped replenish soil moisture after a dangerously dry period, local cooperatives reported.

"Throughout the region there were good rains on Saturday with an average of around 40 millimetres...This should be enough to replenish soil moisture for the next 10 days," said Odair Bachini, agronomist at the Cotricruz cooperative in Cruz Alta.
The rains were the heaviest in the region since before Christmas and meant less of a threat of losses due to the recent dry weather, he added.
"Between now and February, with the crop flowering, we still need regular rains, however," he said.
Temperatures had dipped over the weekend but were expected to pick up again.
In Santa Rosa, the local cooperative also reported around 45 millimetres of rain through Saturday and early Sunday morning.
"We are certainly a lot less worried now although there are no further forecasts of rains for the coming two days," said Gui Omar Backes at the Coopermil cooperative.
In Parana, expected to be the largest soybean-growing state this year, key regions had also seen good rains over the past two days.
"We have no problems here with a lack of rain. Yesterday it rained the whole day," said an agronomist at the Coamo cooperative in Campo Mourao.
In Cascavel the local cooperative also reported no problems with soil moisture and sufficient rainfall.
"It has been raining since Friday. Everything is normal and temperatures are warm, excellent for crop development," said Ernani Campanati of the Coopavel cooperative.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
